A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLIE study. All 18 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments on six datasets, inference-strategy comparisons, computational costs, case studies, and appendix sensitivity and calibration results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports a Zhong et al. baseline across the six datasets in Table 1.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix E retain the same rule generation, ternary judgments, coverage filtering, Elastic Net logistic combiner, hard-example refinement, pruning, and inference procedures. The new comparator does not alter RLIE.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six binary classification tasks: Reviews, Dreaddit, Headlines, Citations, LLM Detect, and Retweets. The added baseline uses this retained coverage; no dataset or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Section 4.2 and Table 1 add Zhong et al. (2024), using natural-language predicate features with a logistic-regression readout, under DeepSeek-V3.2 on all six tasks. This extends the comparison to a closely related approach while retaining every existing comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendices A and C retain the same splits, sample provisions, backbones, metrics, hyperparameters, and calibration procedure. The added comparator is reported within the existing evaluation setup; no distinct protocol or revised setting is documented.

E4.justification: The inference-strategy comparisons, computational cost analysis, rule-evolution and embedding case studies, coverage-threshold sensitivity study, and calibration analysis are retained without changed analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report main-result means over three runs with different random seeds and calibration means with standard deviations over three runs in Table 7. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds six Accuracy/Macro-F1 pairs for Zhong et al., including 66.2/65.9 on Reviews and 48.2/44.1 on Headlines. All previously reported numerical results remain unchanged; these are additional comparator results, not improvements in RLIE's scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, logistic objective, coverage and hard-example formulas in Section 3, and calibration formulas in Appendix C are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about weighted rule learning, hard-example refinement, and separating local LLM judgments from global probabilistic aggregation.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning prompt sensitivity, aggregation reliability, calibration, rule evolution, and compact representations remain unchanged. The discussion and impact statement retain the same applicability considerations and bias-related cautions.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page footnote stating that code is available and supplying a GitHub repository address. v2 lacks this access information. Appendix hyperparameters and prompts are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the repository's contents.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and the bibliography add Zhong et al. (2024), Explaining Datasets in Words: Statistical Models with Natural Language Parameters. The revised positioning acknowledges statistical readouts over natural-language predicates and distinguishes RLIE's adaptive predictive rules from that closely related approach.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized related-work and baseline-description edits, shorter figure captions, added acknowledgments, expanded affiliations, and updated publication and running-header text. The section order and most prose, including appendix content, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a baseline row, Figures 1–2 receive shorter captions, and first-page layout, headers, and some content placement change. The scientific artwork is retained, and appendix pages differ visually only in their running headers.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly strengthens evaluation and research positioning by acknowledging and evaluating a closely related predicate-plus-statistical-readout approach that v2 omitted. The code-access footnote also improves reproducibility information. The gain remains limited: detailed implementation and tuning information for the new comparator is absent, and the existing method, analyses, and conclusions are unchanged.
